_voice: Polite gender-neutral plural forms (ንስኹም), never the gendered singular, Ethiopic script.
_style: Address the user always with the polite gender-neutral plural (ንስኹም: -ኩም/-ኹም suffixes, plural verbs such as ዕቀቡ, ስደዱ, ፈትኑ); never use the gendered singular ንስኻ/ንስኺ or -ካ/-ኪ forms. The couple as a whole is ክልቴኹም (both of you) or ብሓባር (together), e.g. “your story” → “ታሪኽ ክልቴኹም”. The other person is always መጻምድኹም (your partner), never ሰብኣይ/ሰበይቲ/ፈታዊ/ፈታዊት; when a verb would have to agree in gender with the partner or with %@, rephrase so the partner is an object or a possessor (“ካብ %@ መልእኽቲ”, “ናይ %@ ስምዒት”) or use a passive/impersonal form (“መልእኽቲ ተላኢኹ”). The partner-name placeholder %@ is never declined or fused with a prefix/suffix (no ን%@, ብ%@, %@ኡ): write a separate word around it (ናብ %@, ናይ %@) or rephrase. Use Ethiopic script for all text; keep Coupley, Premium, AI, CoupleSync and placeholders (%@, %lld, %1$@) exactly as given, in Latin characters, with a normal space between them and Ethiopic words. Quotes are guillemets « » (inner ‹ ›). Prefer Ethiopic punctuation: ። ends sentences, ፣ is the comma, ፤ the semicolon, ፡ is not used as a word separator (use normal spaces); ? and ! are written directly after the word with no space, and the ellipsis is “…”; keep “ · ” separators and \n as in the source. Numbers use Western digits (1, 2, 3), not Ethiopic numerals; dates come from the system formatter (Gregorian), so never hard-code month names or Ethiopian-calendar dates. Ethiopic has no capital letters, so titles, tabs and buttons need no capitalization; keep buttons short as polite plural imperatives (ዕቀቡ, ሰርዙ, ደጊምኩም ፈትኑ) and titles/tabs as short nouns (ጉዕዞ, ቅጥዕታት). Tigrinya is SOV: put the verb last and don't copy English word order (“Couldn't save” → “ክዕቀብ ኣይተኻእለን”). Plural categories are ["one","other"]: one uses the singular noun (“%lld መዓልቲ”), other the plural (“%lld መዓልትታት”); for counts Tigrinya often keeps the singular after a numeral, which is also acceptable in other. Tone: warm, light and kind, like a friend talking, never flowery or cheesy; avoid literal word-for-word translation and Amharic-only vocabulary.
